Anna (Product): Quick design review — API Keys list + create/rotate/revoke flows. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (section: keys). Looking for accessibility + copy nits and any platform constraints.

Sasha (Design): A few notes from my side: 1) the reveal token modal feels risky — can we avoid showing the raw token after creation? 2) Move the primary CTA to the left on the empty state so it reads as the first action. 3) Warning copy for revoke needs to mention 'last used' and 'cannot be recovered'.

Julio (Frontend): On (1) — we should make the token only shown immediately after creation and never retrievable again. Implementing ephemeral reveal is straightforward, but storing the token in logs is a hard no. We also need an aria-live announcement when the token appears for screen readers.

Taylor (Accessibility): +1 to aria-live. Also keyboard focus: after creating a key, focus should move to the success panel with the copy button. The revoke confirmation dialog must trap focus and have a clear cancel action first. For the table, ensure row actions are reachable via keyboard only (not hover-only menus).

Mike D (Platform): Backend constraints: we already only store hashed tokens, so retrieval after create isn't possible without changing security posture. Ephemeral display on create is fine. Also recommend adding a 'last used' timestamp and 'created by' column in the table — helps surface unused tokens before revoke.

Sasha (Design): UI tweaks: 1) Table filter dropdown — add a 'role' filter (read-only, admin, embed, service) so teams can surface service keys quicker. 2) For mobile narrow widths, hide verbose expiry text and show an icon with tooltip. 3) Revoke modal: add a checkbox "I understand this key will stop working" to reduce accidental clicks. Thoughts?

Julio (Frontend): Checkbox is OK but adds friction. Alternative: make revoke button secondary and the confirm CTA a red button with keyboard-accessible label. If we add a checkbox we need to persist that consent state per session which is extra work.

Taylor (Accessibility): The checkbox approach is fine if it's properly labeled and focusable, but a modal with a clear heading + descriptive paragraph + the red CTA is sufficient for most users. If we add the checkbox, it must be associated with its label and reachable by screen readers (no placeholder text).

Anna (Product): We want to reduce accidental deletes without adding too many clicks. Proposal: combine approaches — modal with clear copy, focus trap, and an optional opt-in checkbox for orgs that enable "strict revokes" in settings (off by default). That keeps default flow light.

Mike D (Platform): Fine from platform POV. For strict revokes we can toggle an org-level flag that adds the checkbox in the UI. Will need a small API change to surface org setting.

Sasha (Design): Copy suggestions for revoke modal: Title: "Revoke API key". Body: "Revoking this key will immediately stop any services using it. Last used: <date>. This action cannot be undone." Buttons: Cancel (secondary), Revoke (danger). Add small helper text: "Consider rotating instead if you need a replacement."

Julio (Frontend): Quick implementation note: the 'last used' cell should be sortable and we should add a keyboard shortcut to open the action menu (e.g., Cmd/Ctrl+K then type key name? maybe too big). For now, support Enter on row to open details.

ops-bot: deployment-tracker: New deploy queued for keys-page v2 at 2024-11-20T14:30Z. CI checks pending :rocket:

Anna (Product): Accessibility nit: make sure the copy-to-clipboard action has a visible success state and an aria-live message "Key copied to clipboard". Also add a tooltip on hover for the masked key: "Click to reveal once".

Sasha (Design): Agree. Also let's avoid showing the full key in any activity logs or screenshots. Add a tiny 'masking' animation when token is displayed so it doesn't pop visually.

Julio (Frontend): I'll implement ephemeral display + aria-live + copy toast. For the masking animation, we can do a short transition CSS. I'll open a PR and tag design and a11y.

Taylor (Accessibility): When you open the PR, please include a keyboard walkthrough in the description (steps to reproduce) and a snippet of the ARIA attributes used. I'll review.

Anna (Product): Thanks all — file follow-up tickets: 1) org-level strict revoke flag (platform), 2) table role filter + last-used column (product + frontend), 3) ephemeral token display + a11y (frontend + a11y). I'll create the tickets and link the PR once it's up. :+1:

Mike D (Platform): noted. I'll add the org flag to the backlog and estimate.

Sasha (Design): Thanks — will push updated Figma screens with the tweak to the empty state CTA and the revoke modal copy by EOD.

Julio (Frontend): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web/pull/1234 — includes ephemeral token display, aria-live, and copy toast. Marking ready for review.

Taylor (Accessibility): Reviewing now. Quick note: ensure color contrast of the danger CTA meets AA (4.5:1) and that the tooltip content is reachable on touch.

Anna (Product): Great — let's merge when a11y and design sign off. Thanks everyone!
